title: Exaramel_Backdoor_Investigation_981
description: You are an incident responder tasked with investigating a potential compromise involving the Exaramel backdoor malware on a Linux-based system. Your goal is to identify, analyze, and contain the threat to prevent further damage.
prerequisites: Basic knowledge of Unix/Linux system administration

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: You are an incident responder tasked with investigating a potential compromise involving the Exaramel backdoor malware on a Linux-based system. Your goal is to identify, analyze, and contain the threat to prevent further damage.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content: Access the target host via SSH using the following credentials: Username: cyrano, Password: cyrano.
levels.local_content: Access the target host via SSH using the following credentials: Username: cyrano, Password: cyrano.

levels.title: Suspicious Service Discovery
levels.content: While monitoring the system, you noticed unusual network activity. Investigate the running services on the target host to identify any unauthorized or suspicious services.
levels.solution: To identify the suspicious service, you can use the command `systemctl list-units --type=service` to list all running services. Look for any services that seem out of place or unfamiliar. The flag is the name of the suspicious service, which in this case is `bkd.service`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Check the list of running services and look for any that seem out of place or unfamiliar.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Use the command `systemctl list-units --type=service` to list all running services.

levels.title: Persistence Discovery
levels.content: Now that you have identified the suspicious service, determine how it is automatically started after a system reboot. This will help you understand the persistence mechanism used by the malware.
levels.solution: To determine the persistence mechanism, you can use the command `systemctl list-timers` to list all systemd timers. Look for any timers that are associated with the suspicious service. The flag is the persistence mechanism used by the suspicious service, which in this case is `lab-checkin.timer`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Investigate systemd services and timers to find how the service is scheduled to run.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Use the command `systemctl list-timers` to list all systemd timers.

levels.title: C2 Communication Discovery (Port)
levels.content: The suspicious service appears to be communicating with an external command-and-control server. Determine which network port is used for this communication to help contain the threat.
levels.solution: To determine the network port used for the suspicious communication, you can use the command `ss -tulnp` to list all listening ports. Look for any ports that are associated with the suspicious service. The flag is the network port used for the suspicious communication, which in this case is `4444`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Analyze network connections and listen ports to identify the suspicious port.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Use the command `ss -tulnp` to list all listening ports.
